name: Product UI micro-interactions (generic)

source.description: Two inspected product promos demonstrate software with typed inputs, cursor clicks, toggles, notification stacks, a long link compressing into a short pill and charts drawing.

technique: Simplified, generic UI fragments perform one interaction each (type, click, toggle, notify, compress) in close-up, so a product's value is shown as action rather than as a screenshot tour.
purpose: Product promos and onboarding: show what the product does in seconds.
visual_behaviour: A URL types itself and shrinks into a short pill; a cursor glides and clicks a button that depresses; toggles flip; cards stack in; a chart line draws with a counter.
mechanics: Typewriter, FLIP width morphs, cursor paths with ease-in-out and a press scale, staggered card entrances, counters.
failure_modes: Recreating a real product's proprietary UI (forbidden without authorisation)
Too much UI detail to read at 720p or on phones

implementation.approach: Generic mock UI components (input, button, toggle, card) in the studio style tokens; typewriter (Studio.type.typewriter), counters (Studio.type.count), pen-led chart lines (Studio.draw.pen). Candidate composition 'ui-mock' for the product-promo template.

priority.note: Highest-value missing piece for the product-promo template.

provenance.observed: A typed long link becomes a short link pill; a dashboard chart draws and switches metrics (approx., from overview spacing).
A link is pasted into an input and submitted with a cursor click; settings toggles flip on a phone mockup.

licensing_notes: Technique only. The references show two companies' proprietary UIs and logos: never reproduce them; use generic, original UI.
